chapters.content: LZ4 operates as a byte-aligned LZ77-family lossless compression algorithm engineered specifically to prioritize raw execution speed over maximum compression ratios. The core compression engine builds a localized hash table directly in memory to track recent byte sequences, mapping incoming byte streams to previously encountered match offsets with minimal algorithmic overhead. This design choice shifts the bottleneck from complex CPU instruction pipelines directly to main memory bandwidth. Decompression is exceptionally lean, executing as a straightforward sequence of literal copies and match duplications driven by explicit length tokens. Because the decompression grammar is strictly unambiguous and requires virtually no branch prediction state, it consistently achieves multi-gigabyte per second throughput on modern CPU cores. The memory footprint during both compression and decompression is exceptionally modest, requiring only a tiny working memory state that easily fits entirely within modern processor L1 and L2 cache hierarchies. This eliminates cache thrashing and guarantees predictable execution latencies, making it an ideal choice for high-frequency trading platforms, real-time telemetry streaming pipelines, and high-throughput database journaling systems where latency spikes are completely unacceptable.

chapters.title: Architectural Foundation & Execution Mechanics
chapters.content: Pushary for Teams operates as a centralized proprietary oversight platform designed to intercept, log, and govern human-in-the-loop decisions generated by decentralized AI agent pipelines. This decoupling of agent execution from the governance plane ensures that latency introduced by human latency does not disrupt local process loops, while maintaining an immutable audit log across disparate multi-agent frameworks. By centralizing decision states, the architecture mitigates the pervasive blind spot of fragmented agent logs, replacing ad-hoc internal webhook integrations with a standardized oversight broker.
